title: Platform racer with Astra 6
author: BackgroundAd5676
selftext:
For the past two days, I've created a platform racer game for my kids to play against each other. Supports local or network based play up to a maximum of 4 players.

Basically, its a platform game where the main objective is to reach first to the end of the level. Levels are randomly generated and there are 6 different powerups randomly spawn, that allows players to use them in a strategic way in order to get the best of the opponents. 

I had a lot of fun doing this little project. Playable in the browser. Just wanted to do a small showcase. Fell free to ask anything about it. 

It uses node.js and three.js. Only used ChatGPT Plus and it took me several sessions to iterate on the project. Had a couple of ideias from my kids, watching them play and improved upon this. All the assets, audio and code are AI generated, allowing me to focus on design and gameplay.

comments.author: soulglider26
comments.body:
Making games for your kids to play is PEAK. Last year for xmas I made a game for my brother to play with my niece since I live far away.

I'm not sure how much you know about level design, but adding some simple objects that get in your way, forcing more climb/fall sequences between platforms can vary the racing a lot!

replies.author: BackgroundAd5676
replies.body: Yeah they loved it and are very happy to be part of the design. The game has three types of obstacles (saw, laser beams and spikes), three types of enemies (flyers, patrollers and turrets) and four types of platforms (ice, drop, moving and fixed). With the six types of power ups, the whole random generated levels, the race factor since the game has 5 min to finish, there is a lot of strategy and competition. Overall I am happy with the result and even tested it with other family members as well.
